key_insight: A highly simplified two-parameter model, DynaBase, can still perform strong zero-shot reconstruction of dynamical systems by blending the current latent state with nearest in-context neighbors and their successors.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that interpretable, low-parameter architectures can rival large foundation models for dynamical-system forecasting while enabling direct optimization and closed-form analysis.
method: Iteratively reduced the DynaMix foundation model to a minimal interpretable form.
Used a linear blend of the current latent state, nearest context neighbor, and its temporal successor for forecasting.
Analyzed a 1-parameter family of maps to connect reconstruction behavior with contextual-parroting and chaotic regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports competitive zero-shot reconstruction across chaotic and cyclic systems, with negligible parameter count and evaluation tied to reconstruction and prediction MSE.
watch_item: The simplicity that improves interpretability may also make performance sensitive to context selection and training objective, especially when optimizing for short-term prediction versus full reconstruction.
paper_title: A Minimal Interpretable Architecture for Zero-Shot Reconstruction of Dynamical Systems
